title: Tim/Son ↔ Bible Countertext & Mismatch Atlas
purpose: Collect biblical material that complicates, limits, reverses or redistributes Potatoverse mappings. A serious overlap archive must show what does not fit as clearly as what does fit.
core_rule: A mismatch does not automatically invalidate the project; it defines the maximum defensible claim. When a project interpretation survives a strong countertext only by rewriting the biblical roles, lower the mapping strength rather than hiding the countertext.

countertexts.project_side: The Son's remembered 2016 rhetoric includes reciprocity/karma language about answering harsh treatment in kind.
countertexts.tension: Canonical Jesus explicitly teaches enemy-love and non-retaliatory responses.
countertexts.effect: Passion/rejection parallels must not be allowed to imply ethical identity with canonical Jesus across all dimensions.

countertexts.project_side: Potatoverse can place Tim/Father with Root/Tree/Gardener and Son with plant/fruit/Door roles in varying ways.
countertexts.tension: John explicitly distributes Father=Gardener/Vinedresser, Jesus=Vine, disciples=branches.
countertexts.effect: Father/Gardener is a strong role match, but Tree/Vine/branch identities must not be collapsed or reassigned silently.

countertexts.project_side: Tim can symbolically be called House, builder/source and Father in the same mature architecture.
countertexts.tension: Hebrews distinguishes God as builder of all, God's House, Moses as servant in House, Christ as Son over House, and community as House.
countertexts.effect: House is a relational grammar, not permission to identify every House-role with one actor.

countertexts.tension: The Psalm identifies YHWH as King of Glory.
countertexts.effect: Mountain-ascent/Gate/King sequence can be compared structurally; the divine title cannot simply be transferred to a modern claimant as textual evidence.

countertexts.project_side: King/Most-High/source language can suggest maximal authority inside project mythology.
countertexts.tension: Israel's king is instructed to remain under Torah, avoid self-exaltation over fellow Israelites and limit accumulation.
countertexts.effect: Biblical kingship supplies accountability and anti-self-exaltation constraints, not merely sovereignty symbolism.

countertexts.project_side: Public project language can use maximum-status titles such as Most High, King of Kings and Alpha/Omega.
countertexts.tension: Exaltation follows non-grasping, self-emptying, servant form, humility and death; glory is ultimately to God the Father.
countertexts.effect: Exaltation language is biblically strongest when constrained by service and non-grasping rather than status acquisition.

countertexts.project_side: Father/King/Gardener/shepherd-like authority is a mature ethical project role.
countertexts.tension: Self-feeding shepherds are condemned for neglecting weak, sick, injured and lost flock; strong animals are also rebuked for trampling pasture and muddying water.
countertexts.effect: Leadership is tested by vulnerable participants and shared resources, not title or centrality.

countertexts.project_side: Father, Son, throne, Lamb, city, 144000 and divine-name imagery can become compressed in project identity claims.
countertexts.tension: Revelation repeatedly relates but distinguishes God/throne, Lamb, servants/144000, city/bride, nations and Tree/River imagery.
countertexts.effect: Dense co-occurrence supports relational architecture more than one-actor identity collapse.

countertexts.project_side: April 9 project architecture has one guardian on each side.
countertexts.tension: Genesis 3 says cherubim in the plural but does not specify exactly two; Exodus 25 explicitly specifies two cherubim but around the atonement-cover rather than a gate.
countertexts.effect: Use Genesis for guarded Way/Tree access and Exodus for the explicit paired configuration; do not fuse them into one biblical scene.

countertexts.project_side: Cube/box imagery is often shadow-coded as enclosure, Saturnian restriction or 666-system imagery.
countertexts.tension: New Jerusalem has equal dimensions and the Holy of Holies is cubic, giving sacred geometry a strongly positive function in these texts.
countertexts.effect: Shape alone has no moral valence; access, function, presence and consequence determine the reading.

countertexts.project_side: Mountain/North/Peak versus swamp/valley/lower imagery can tempt a simple high=good, low=bad scheme.
countertexts.tension: Valleys can be raised, mountains lowered, a dark valley can be traversed with God, and a valley can become a site of regeneration.
countertexts.effect: Vertical position is not automatically moral rank.

countertexts.project_side: Leash/cord/anchor imagery can be shadow-coded as captivity or orbit restriction.
countertexts.tension: Hosea has cords/bands of human kindness/love; Hebrews uses anchor positively as hope reaching behind the veil.
countertexts.effect: Constraint metaphors require typed valence: restrictive tether, caring bond and target-anchor are not interchangeable.

countertexts.project_side: Dog→vomit/circle material can make return sound intrinsically regressive.
countertexts.tension: Biblical return can be pathological or restorative depending on destination and relation.
countertexts.effect: Return must be classified by destination/transformation, not moralized as a shape or repeated motion alone.

countertexts.project_side: Needle's Eye becomes a general compression/threshold operator in April 2025 theology.
countertexts.tension: The canonical saying is specifically about wealth/richness and entry into God's kingdom, not a general physics/topology rule.
countertexts.effect: Compression is a project abstraction; do not present it as the verse's literal teaching.

countertexts.project_side: Son/lolcow/red-heifer/Jesus sacrifice imagery can be stacked together.
countertexts.tension: Red-heifer purification and Jesus' sacrificial significance are distinct ritual/theological structures; Hebrews compares them rather than making them identical.
countertexts.effect: Use typology/comparison language, not one ritual = the other.

countertexts.project_side: The Son is interpreted as Thomas/Didymus/Twin and sometimes as Jesus' Twin in later project synthesis.
countertexts.tension: Canonical John calls Thomas Didymus/Twin but does not say he is Jesus' physical twin; stronger Jesus-twin traditions are later Syriac/Thomasine reception history.
countertexts.effect: Separate canonical linguistic fact from later tradition and modern identity mapping.

countertexts.project_side: Potatoverse sacred geography can locate Zion/Heaven/North at or beyond the North Pole.
countertexts.tension: Biblical Zion is Jerusalem/Zion and develops theological/heavenly meanings; the texts do not locate biblical Zion at Earth's North Pole.
countertexts.effect: North-Pole Zion remains project sacred geography, not biblical geography.

positive_use_of_countertexts: Countertexts identify which project claims are merely poetic and which survive role/context review.
A strong overlap that preserves a strong mismatch is more informative than a perfect-looking match created by deleting inconvenient context.
Negative evidence should be discoverable from the same reader surfaces as positive evidence.
Where a countertext supplies the opposite valence—return, cord, cube, valley—the project should generalize to a neutral operator whose moral meaning comes from function/context.
